topic: The minimax bracket and exact no-penalty phase for testing treatment-effect heterogeneity with rough confounding. For fixed d>=1, alpha,beta,gamma>0, Holder radius L>=2, and overlap epsilon in (0,1/4), observe n iid O=(X,A,Y), with X uniform on [0,1]^d, A binary, Y in [0,1], propensity e in H^alpha(L) satisfying epsilon<=e<=1-epsilon, baseline mu0=E[Y|A=0,X] in H^beta(L), and CATE tau=mu1-mu0 in H^gamma(L). Consistency and conditional exchangeability identify tau; the experiment is the observed-data image of the corresponding full causal-law class. No interior arm-mean restriction, conditional-variance floor, or fitted-nuisance rate is assumed. Let V(P)=integral (tau-integral tau)^2 and rho_star(n) be the constant-CATE minimax separation radius at size 0.05 and type-II error 0.20 over this same observed-law class. Prove the full-class two-sided bracket c*r_or(n)<=rho_star(n)<=C*max(r_or(n),r_nu(n)), with explicit powers r_or=n^(-2gamma/(4gamma+d)) and r_nu=n^(-4gamma(alpha+beta)/(4gamma(alpha+beta)+d(alpha+beta)+2dgamma)). Prove the exact no-penalty phase rho_star(n) asymptotic to r_or(n) when alpha+beta>=2dgamma/(4gamma+d), including equality without logarithmic loss. Supply an explicitly computable, terminating, uniformly calibrated higher-order corrected-energy test attaining the upper endpoint, with deterministic tuning from the declared class constants and stated arithmetic complexity. Treat only the complementary rough regime alpha+beta<2dgamma/(4gamma+d) as open: whether r_nu is sharp, whether alpha and beta enter separately through further elbows, and whether logarithms occur there. Compare this continuous-design CATE-variance testing problem locally with the discrete arbitrary-cell-mass scalar-ATE bracket stat_discrete_ate_heterogeneity_frontier/v1 and with the additional learner/direction/variance conditions of Yu (2026) and Dhawan--Guo--Shah (2026), without claiming those procedures give a uniform full-class minimax converse.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp minimax separation radius for testing constant CATE against Hölder-smooth variance-separated alternatives when both propensity and baseline regression are unknown and may be too rough for first-order product-rate conditions.

source_refs.claim: Their observational effect-modifier test has power when the learned direction correlates with the true score, but does not characterize an omnibus minimax separation radius.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest constant-CATE procedures establish size and power under direction-correlation or nuisance-rate conditions, while the closest minimax causal result concerns CATE estimation. A sharp test must profile an unknown constant effect, control drift from two rough nuisance functions, and remain calibratable through degeneracy without relative spectral consistency. Its converse must use full observed-data mixtures—not score marginals—whose null components retain constant CATE, exact uniform design, overlap, and bounded outcomes. Prior work supplies pieces of higher-order correction, mixed calibration, and common-support lower bounds, but not their same-class combination or the resulting phase boundaries.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise explicit rate r_n(alpha,beta,gamma,d), including equality-case logarithms, together with a terminating data-computable uniformly level-0.05 test attaining it and matching full-observation composite-null lower bounds for all tests.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from semiparametric score testing to observational effect-modifier detection and exposes the dependence of power on the hunted direction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Classical score tests require a specified direction -> flexible regression hypotheses require hunting and debiasing a direction -> constant-CATE testing needs an omnibus frontier when no learned direction is guaranteed to correlate with heterogeneity.

method_exemplars.technique: Localized fuzzy-hypothesis lower bounds and a higher-order local-polynomial R-learner separating target smoothness from propensity and outcome-regression smoothness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It handles the same Hölder causal nuisance geometry and proves a genuine nuisance-driven minimax elbow.

method_exemplars.technique: A first-difference proxy statistic with matching minimax upper and lower bounds across mean- and variance-smoothness regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Heteroskedasticity testing is an analogous constant-versus-varying conditional-functional problem in which rough regression nuisance changes detection.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimized linear U-test weights for a composite null defined by a nonnegative quadratic functional, with sharp minimax separation constants.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Profiled CATE variance is a positive quadratic functional with a nontrivial kernel; this is the direct benchmark after removing causal nuisance.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether a proxy-energy statistic analogous to optimal first-difference heteroskedasticity tests can improve the rough-nuisance constant-CATE detection rate over corrected direct estimation of Var(tau(X)) under unrestricted bounded conditional outcome laws.

source_refs.claim: For nonparametric heteroskedasticity testing, the sharp rate can be attained by estimating a proxy rather than the natural variance-function distance from constants.
source_refs.author: Subhodh Kotekal, Soumyabrata Kundu

source_refs.claim: Higher-order pathwise differentiability yields nuisance-adjusted U-statistic omnibus tests for equality of unknown functions, including a zero-CATE special case.
source_refs.author: Alex Luedtke, Marco Carone, Mark J. van der Laan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.claim: Direct CATE-variance inference is nonregular at homogeneity, and ordinary splitting of squared doubly robust scores destroys the intended first-order bias cancellation.
source_refs.author: Fangzhou Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The donor heteroskedasticity construction uses identities for squared regression differences and, in its roughest regime, distributional information about Gaussian noise. In the causal destination, treatment assignment adds an unknown propensity, the two arm means enter asymmetrically, and the conditional outcome law is unrestricted beyond boundedness. The donor's first proof step—turning a local squared difference into an unbiased proxy for variation—therefore fails and must be replaced by treatment-weighted cross-products with uniformly controlled nuisance drift.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a proxy-functional CATE test with a proved phasewise minimax separation rate and matching full-class lower bound, or a counterexample theorem showing that unrestricted bounded outcome noise prevents any proxy improvement over corrected direct energy estimation.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames CATE variance as the natural omnibus target and isolates null degeneracy and nonlinear nuisance bias as the central obstruction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE heterogeneity is summarized by its variance -> the variance degenerates at homogeneity and naive splitting breaks orthogonality -> seek an observable proxy with sharper rough-confounding behavior.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace direct quadratic-functional estimation by a squared-difference proxy, then match its bias and variance using null-preserving minimax mixtures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems test constancy of a conditional function in the presence of a distinct rough conditional-mean nuisance.

method_exemplars.technique: Use second-order pathwise differentiation under a degenerate null to construct nuisance-adjusted U-statistics and calibrate their null law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly treats unknown causal regression functions and shows how null degeneracy creates exploitable higher-order structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Truncated higher-order influence-function U-statistics with an explicit approximation-bias versus stochastic-variance tradeoff.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired proxy test also concerns a nonlinear causal functional when first-order nuisance products are too large.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct one uniformly valid rough-confounding heterogeneity test that is simultaneously rate-optimal for learned-direction alternatives and dense Hölder L2 alternatives, and characterize the two minimax boundaries over their union.

source_refs.claim: Hunt-and-test has power when the learned direction correlates with the true score, leaving poorly aligned signals outside its stated power guarantee.
source_refs.author: Aditya Dhawan, F. Richard Guo, Rajen D. Shah

source_refs.claim: Projected covariance turns conditional-mean dependence into a learned-projection test, and a spline implementation attains a minimax rate under stated smoothness conditions.
source_refs.author: Anton Rask Lundborg, Ilmun Kim, Rajen D. Shah, Richard J. Samworth

source_refs.claim: Dense smooth alternatives to quadratic-functional nulls are handled by optimally weighted U-tests with matching minimax lower bounds.
source_refs.author: Laetitia Comminges, Arnak S. Dalalyan

open_problems.why_unsolved: A first-order test can detect a small signal when a learned direction has substantial correlation but can be powerless against energy dispersed over many nearly orthogonal coefficients. A quadratic omnibus test covers dense signals but pays an effective-dimension variance cost and can be inferior on aligned alternatives. Combining them is not routine under rough confounding because the statistics share learned nuisances and profiling estimates, while their least-favorable alternatives can occupy different nuisance phases.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Two alternative-class-specific minimax separation formulas and a single data-computable level-0.05 hybrid test attaining the oracle minimum up to constants over their union, with a matching lower bound for adaptation between aligned and dense regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its hunt-and-test narrative motivates both the statistical benefit and the limitation of concentrating power along a learned alternative direction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Omnibus tests spread power over many directions -> machine learning can hunt a promising effect-modifier direction -> a complete procedure should retain directional gains without losing minimax power against dense heterogeneity.

method_exemplars.technique: Sample-split learning of a projection followed by a studentized conditional-covariance statistic, with a spline specialization and minimax lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a proved bridge between learned-direction power and minimax conditional-mean testing.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimally weighted quadratic U-tests for dense ellipsoidal alternatives and extremal-prior lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the natural dense-energy component to combine with a learned-direction score.

method_exemplars.technique: Independent hunt/test splitting and weighted-least-squares debiasing of a score evaluated along a machine-learned direction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly supplies the aligned-alternative component and its observational nuisance correction.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend sharp rough-confounding detection theory from the constant-CATE null to the composite null that tau belongs to a known q-dimensional linear function space, including regimes where q grows with n.

source_refs.claim: The debiased-score framework tests membership in a specified linear regression class and includes observational effect-modifier testing, but its power theorem is directional rather than minimax.
source_refs.author: Aditya Dhawan, F. Richard Guo, Rajen D. Shah

source_refs.claim: For ordinary nonparametric regression, sharp minimax tests exist for composite nulls that are kernels of diagonal quadratic functionals.
source_refs.author: Laetitia Comminges, Arnak S. Dalalyan

source_refs.claim: The classical econometric test treats zero or constant conditional average treatment effects but does not give a rough-nuisance minimax phase diagram.
source_refs.author: Richard K. Crump, V. Joseph Hotz, Guido W. Imbens, Oscar A. Mitnik

open_problems.why_unsolved: In direct regression, projection off a known q-dimensional null space produces a quadratic functional with a known kernel. In observational causal data, projected CATE coefficients require propensity and baseline correction, and estimating the null-space coefficients changes both degenerate covariance and nuisance remainder. When q grows, profiling error can interact with the higher-order truncation scale, so neither the q=1 boundary nor the direct-regression formula transfers.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax characterization r_n(alpha,beta,gamma,d,q) with explicit q-growth regimes, an implementable projected higher-order test with uniform size, and a matching lower bound whose null mixtures all have CATE in the declared linear space.

writing_exemplar.why: It naturally formulates semiparametric goodness-of-fit as membership in a linear function class and specializes that framework to effect modification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scientific nulls often constrain a regression function to a linear class -> debiased scores test selected departures in semiparametric models -> determine the omnibus boundary for CATE departures from a possibly growing causal null space.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent the composite null as the kernel of a diagonal quadratic functional, optimize its linear U-test, and construct sharp least-favorable alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Projection of tau off the known null space produces precisely such a positive-semidefinite quadratic functional before causal correction.

method_exemplars.technique: Higher-order local-polynomial R-learning with localized fuzzy hypotheses under separately smooth propensity, baseline, and CATE functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies causal machinery for replacing directly observed regression coefficients by nuisance-corrected CATE coefficients.

method_exemplars.technique: Empirical higher-order influence-function correction using an independently estimated Gram operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Growing-null-space profiling and large basis truncations require stable empirical projection corrections of this form.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the unavoidable adaptation penalty for one honest constant-CATE test that does not know alpha, beta, or gamma and competes with the oracle sharp detection rate over prescribed Hölder-smoothness ranges.

source_refs.claim: Adaptive nonparametric signal detection cannot retain the fixed-smoothness rate without loss; a log-log factor is unavoidable over broad Besov classes.
source_refs.author: Vladimir G. Spokoiny

source_refs.claim: Multiple quadratic-distance tests adapt to optimal L2 goodness-of-fit rates for simple nulls, while composite families can incur logarithmic loss.
source_refs.author: Magalie Fromont, Béatrice Laurent

source_refs.claim: Multivariate uniform-design regression tests achieve sharp asymptotics over smooth ellipsoids but are inherently nonadaptive.
source_refs.author: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical adaptation theory treats a directly observed regression or density signal. Here the oracle rate may switch between target-smoothness and nuisance-limited phases, while the null contains an unknown constant and unknown propensity and baseline functions. A multiscale maximum must be calibrated uniformly over nuisance estimates, and its lower bound must separate the ordinary cost of adapting to gamma from any additional cost of not knowing which nuisance phase applies.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adaptive minimax theorem giving the exact phasewise logarithmic or iterated-logarithmic multiplier relative to the fixed-(alpha,beta,gamma) boundary, with one data-computable multiscale test and a matching adaptive lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates adaptation through simultaneous quadratic-distance tests and distinguishes simple-null from composite-null penalties.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Oracle quadratic tests depend on unknown regularity -> aggregate tests across resolutions while preserving level -> identify the precise adaptation price under a composite constant-CATE null with nuisance-driven phase changes.

method_exemplars.technique: Wavelet multiscale aggregation paired with a mixture lower bound proving the inevitability of a log-log adaptation cost.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The alternatives are L2-separated and indexed by unknown smoothness, the canonical geometry where adaptive detection differs from adaptive estimation.

method_exemplars.technique: Finite-level multiple testing of U-statistic squared-distance estimators with nonasymptotic level allocation over resolutions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Corrected CATE-energy tests likewise generate a family of resolution-indexed quadratic statistics needing simultaneous conservative calibration.

method_exemplars.technique: Sharp extremal weighting of projected coefficients and Gaussian asymptotics for multivariate random uniform-design regression.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the oracle known-design benchmark against which the causal adaptation penalty should be measured.

literature_map:
Dhawan, Guo and Shah (2026, arXiv:2607.28861) give a debiased hunt-and-test score for semiparametric regression classes and observational effect modifiers; power requires correlation with the hunted direction, not an omnibus minimax characterization.
Yu (2026, arXiv:2607.17451) targets Var(CATE), identifies null degeneracy and a sample-splitting failure of orthogonality, and proposes intra-fold splitting with asymptotic normality rather than a Hölder minimax frontier.
Dukes, Stensrud, Brioschi and Hudson (2024, arXiv:2410.00985) develop quantitative and qualitative nonparametric homogeneity tests with fixed and local asymptotics, but not a rough-confounding minimax boundary.
Crump, Hotz, Imbens and Mitnik (2008, Review of Economics and Statistics, DOI:10.1162/rest.90.3.389) are the classical zero-or-constant-CATE testing anchor under unconfoundedness.
Levy, van der Laan, Hubbard and Pirracchio (2021, Journal of Causal Inference, DOI:10.1515/jci-2019-0003) formalize CATE variance and provide TMLE and CV-TMLE efficiency conditions; boundary degeneracy remains central for testing.
Sanchez-Becerra (2023, arXiv:2306.03363) develops boundary-robust VCATE confidence intervals for experiments using higher-order limiting behavior rather than an observational nonparametric detection boundary.
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/24-AOS2369) establish a Hölder minimax CATE-estimation frontier with a nuisance-smoothness elbow and localized fuzzy hypotheses.
Gao and Han (2020, arXiv:2002.06471) provide another minimax CATE-estimation benchmark emphasizing smooth effect differences over rougher baselines; it is estimation rather than homogeneity detection.
Lundborg, Kim, Shah and Samworth (2024, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/24-AOS2447) prove minimax conditional-mean-independence testing for a spline projected-covariance measure, a close directional analogue.
Luedtke, Carone and van der Laan (2019, JRSSB, DOI:10.1111/rssb.12299) use higher-order differentiability and U-statistics for omnibus equality tests of unknown functions, including a zero-CATE special case.
Robins, Li, Mukherjee, Tchetgen Tchetgen and van der Vaart (2017, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/16-AOS1515), and Liu, Mukherjee, Newey and Robins (2017, arXiv:1705.07577), supply higher-order influence-function and empirical-projection machinery for low-regularity nuisances.
Kotekal and Kundu (2025, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/24-AOS2467) derive sharp heteroskedasticity-detection rates with rough mean nuisance and show that a proxy statistic can be optimal.
Comminges and Dalalyan (2013, Electronic Journal of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/13-EJS766) give sharp U-tests and minimax constants for composite nulls defined by quadratic functionals in regression.
Ingster and Sapatinas (2009, Mathematical Methods of Statistics, DOI:10.3103/S1066530709030041) supply the multivariate uniform-design known-regression benchmark; their tests are explicitly nonadaptive.
Spokoiny (1996, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/aos/1032181163) and Fromont and Laurent (2006, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/009053606000000119) establish classical adaptation losses for multiscale L2 testing, unresolved for nuisance-driven causal phase transitions.
prior_proposal_map:
Mined active and banked artifacts under CausalSmith/doc/research, prioritizing adjacent statistical minimax and degeneracy runs.
The active stat_cot_boundary_degeneracy_frontier run yielded unresolved observable-calibration and relative-spectrum obstructions relevant to degenerate quadratic CATE statistics.
Its projected-energy writeups also supplied the technique-derived need to rework kernel covariance and profiling under causal nuisance correction.
The stat_bdd_thickness_estimability_frontier artifact identified the lower-bound legality failure of relying on a score projection instead of full observed-data distance.
The exp_ani_annealed_hac_exactness artifact supplied a transferable common-support construction strategy, though its finite-cell experiment must be rebuilt for exact uniform continuous X and constant-CATE null mixtures.
Inspected available reviews/*.json; none contained a strengthening_paths entry directly resolving the CATE frontier.
No relevant archived rejected-angle proposal supplied a distinct surviving opportunity after cross-track merging.
The three Track-A directions—calibration, corrected energy construction, and legal lower bounds—were merged with the web-supported sharp-frontier opportunity rather than counted separately.
